title: Personal LLM mini tracker (Feb 2026)
content:
Quick personal mini-sheet for ongoing LLM experiment runs. Kept intentionally lightweight so I can copy/paste rows into a proper sheet later. Mostly measuring throughput/latency/cost tradeoffs and a quick subjective quality score for a small eval set.

Columns: Date | Exp ID | Model | Prompt brief | Temp | MaxSeq | Batch size | Avg latency (ms/token) | Cost (USD/token) | Quality (0-5) | Notes

Rows (most recent first):
2026-02-19 | EXP-122 | redwood-mix-1.3b-q4 | summarization-short | 0.2 | 256 | 8 | 12.4 ms | 0.0009 | 4.1 | small batch gives good latency; try caching prefixes next
2026-02-18 | EXP-121 | redwood-mix-1.3b-fp16 | summarization-short | 0.2 | 256 | 8 | 9.8 ms | 0.0011 | 4.2 | fp16 slightly faster but higher cost due to memory pressure causing more frequent micro-batches
2026-02-15 | EXP-120 | open-llama-3b-8bit | summarization-short | 0.2 | 256 | 4 | 18.6 ms | 0.00045 | 3.8 | quantized variant cheaper but quality dip on long tails
2026-02-12 | EXP-118 | redwood-mix-1.3b-q4 | open-domain-chat | 0.7 | 512 | 1 | 22.1 ms | 0.0012 | 3.9 | single-stream low throughput, good for latency SLO per user
2026-02-11 | EXP-115 | redwood-mix-1.3b-q4 | instruction-follow | 0.0 | 128 | 16 | 6.7 ms | 0.00085 | 4.4 | large batch ideal for background jobs

Quick metrics (last 10 runs):
- Median latency (ms/token): 11.2
- Median cost (USD/token): 0.00095
- Median quality score: 4.05

Notes / hypotheses:
- q4 quantization (redwood-mix-1.3b-q4) consistently reduces cost but sometimes introduces small hallucination failures on long contexts. Need a focused eval on knowledge consistency for >512 tokens.
- Batching of 8 appears to be a good sweet spot for interactive throughput for this model family. Batching >8 gives diminishing returns for latency-sensitive routes.
- FP16 paths show nicer latency but need memory tuning; observed micro-batch fallback which increases token cost. Investigate allocator flags.
- For chat use-cases with >512 context, try KV-prefix caching; add a small experiment to compare cold vs warm cache latency.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- [ ] Add a small eval harness: 50 edge-case prompts to score hallucination rate across redwood-mix-1.3b-q4 vs fp16 vs 8bit. (target: 2026-02-26)
- [ ] Run warm vs cold cache test for 512+ contexts (EXP-125).
- [ ] Add a column for "warm cache latency" and "cold cache latency" to track cache benefits over time.
- [ ] Pull cost per-token from billing export and add a weekly rolling average automation.

Scratch notes / personal reminders:
- Keep this sheet minimal; once experiments stabilize I'll migrate to shared spreadsheet under eng/applied-ml.
- Ping Maya for help reproducing FP16 micro-batch fallback (Slack thread: #infra-kernel).
- Add a small script to convert these rows into CSV for quick import into the benchmarking dashboard.

Past quick links: confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/LLM+Experiments+Hub | jira: FS-3421 | slack: #model-performance
short_description: Personal lightweight tracker for LLM inference experiments focusing on latency/cost/quality tradeoffs. Draft notes and TODOs.
